headline: Trainable, but 5 images lack label files — 2 of them in val, which silently corrupts your validation mAP. Fix those before training; everything else is cosmetic.
training_impact: The run will start and finish: 596/598 images have labels, all 6,696 boxes are in-bounds and normalised, class ids are valid, and there is no train/val leakage. The cost is measurement, not training: Ultralytics treats an image with no .txt as a pure background image. The 2 missing val labels (val/000000223182, val/000000549220) mean any objects in those frames are scored as correctly-predicted background, inflating your val mAP — the number you will use to decide whether the model is good. The 3 missing train labels teach the model that whatever is in those frames is background, suppressing recall for those classes.

decisions.rationale: 5 images have no label file (exact detector, verified: the .txt files are absent on disk). Fix first: look at the 2 val images. If they contain objects, annotate them — otherwise your val mAP is inflated by uncounted ground truth. If they are genuinely empty scenes, create empty .txt files so the intent is explicit. Same for the 3 train images: annotate or create empty files; as-is, the model is being told those frames are background.

3 train label files exist but contain zero rows. If these are deliberate background/negative images, leave them — that is a legitimate technique. If the annotations were lost, the model is silently learning false negatives. Worth a 2-minute visual check; no action blocks training.
3 label files with no matching image. They are never read during training, so zero impact on the model — pure hygiene. Delete them (or restore the images if they were deleted by mistake).
